title: Kent Beck and the Origins of Test-Driven Development
explainer: Test-driven development was popularized by Kent Beck as part of Extreme Programming in the late 1990s and formalized in his 2002 book 'Test-Driven Development: By Example' - the write-the-failing-test-first discipline taught in this lesson traces directly to that work. Beck had earlier written SUnit, a testing framework for Smalltalk, with Erich Gamma, and that lineage led to the xUnit family (JUnit among them) that most modern testing frameworks still follow. Treating TDD as a specific, named methodology rather than generic 'good practice' helps explain why different teams apply its discipline with different degrees of strictness.
